subject: rider
name: Safe Handling & Restraint
summary: Approaching, moving around, reading basic body language, and tying or restraining a horse safely.
purpose: Prevents preventable injuries to both horse and handler during everyday care and preparation.
safety: Announce your voice and touch at the shoulder before moving into blind spots directly in front of the nose or behind the hindquarters.
Never wrap a lead rope around your hands, wrists, or waist, and never tie a horse by bridle reins or a non-breakaway setup.
Use a solid tie ring at or above wither height with a quick-release knot or breakaway link, leaving exits clear if a horse startles.

introductory.overview: Safe positioning, predictable touch, and reliable quick-release tying around a calm, cooperative horse.

components.title: Approaching, moving, and blind-spot safety
components.description: Reading initial posture from a safe distance, approaching toward the shoulder, keeping one hand quietly along the hip when crossing close behind (or giving wide clearance outside kick range), and keeping stall doors and exits unblocked.

components.title: Rope handling and safe tying
components.description: Holding excess rope neatly folded rather than coiled around fingers, adjusting tie length so a horse cannot step a hoof over the rope, and tying a quick-release knot or using an approved panic/breakaway link at wither height or higher.

components.title: Common mistakes and welfare check
components.description: Common mistakes include darting silently into blind spots, pinning oneself between horse and wall, or tying low to flimsy rails. Notice ear, breathing, and muscle-bracing cues rather than assuming stillness means relaxation.

introductory.learning: Approaches and ties a quiet horse safely with occasional reminders on blind spots, rope folds, tie length, or exit positioning.
introductory.proficient: Independently approaches, moves around, and ties a cooperative horse safely—keeping hands free of rope loops, maintaining clear escape paths, and setting safe tie height, length, and release hardware.

intermediate.overview: Adapting handling, holding, and restraint choices thoughtfully for anxious, green, painful, or unfamiliar horses and busy settings.

components.title: Distinguishing freeze from genuine calm
components.description: Recognizing early sympathetic arousal (high head, fixed eye, held breath, tight muzzle, weight shifting onto hindquarters) as well as quiet shutdown/freeze before a sudden explosion occurs.

components.title: Choosing appropriate holding or restraint
components.description: Deciding when a horse is safest held by a competent handler on a loose lead instead of tied or cross-tied—especially in new venues, medical moments, or around startled horses—and organizing bystanders safely.

intermediate.learning: Adjusts restraint and positioning for mild tension or busy venues with occasional coaching on timing or bystander placement.
intermediate.proficient: Independently reads early tension or freeze responses, selects safe holding or tying arrangements fitted to the horse and environment, and manages space calmly to protect horse and bystanders.

subject: rider
name: Grooming
summary: Keeping a horse's coat, skin, mane, tail, and hooves clean and healthy while noticing changes in condition.
purpose: Supports equine comfort and hygiene, builds handling confidence, and serves as the primary daily check for injuries or abnormalities.
safety: Stay balanced at the horse's side rather than kneeling on both knees or sitting directly behind hooves.
Adjust brush pressure to coat thickness and sensitive areas, watch wash-rack footing, and protect warm muscles from chilling after bathing.

introductory.overview: Safe, thorough everyday grooming, four-hoof picking, and recognizing obvious skin, limb, or hoof concerns on a cooperative horse.

components.title: Coat, face, mane, and tail care
components.description: Matching brush stiffness to body region—light touch around head, belly, and lower legs—working with hair growth, and detangling tails from the bottom up without yanking hair roots.

components.title: Safe hoof picking and sole check
components.description: Standing beside the shoulder or hip facing rearward without kneeling, sliding a hand smoothly down the leg, supporting weight comfortably, picking heel-to-toe around the frog, and spotting thrush odor, packed stones, cracks, or loose shoes.

components.title: Common mistakes and obvious health flags
components.description: Avoid scrubbing hard over bony prominences or using dirty tools across horses. Spot fresh cuts, abnormal heat, noticeable swelling, saddle/girth rubs, or sudden flinching and report them promptly.

introductory.learning: Grooms and picks hooves on a cooperative horse with reminders about brush selection, safe stance, or spotting minor rubs and debris.
introductory.proficient: Independently grooms a cooperative horse gently and thoroughly, picks all four hooves safely with good body mechanics, maintains clean tools, and catches and reports obvious rubs, heat, swelling, or hoof issues.

intermediate.overview: Adapting grooming, safe bathing/drying, seasonal skin care, and subtle soundness/condition checks to the individual horse and weather.

components.title: Weather-smart bathing, rinsing, and drying
components.description: Checking air temperature, wind, and shelter before bathing; introducing water calmly from hooves upward; rinsing soap residue completely to prevent skin irritation; scraping thoroughly; and walking or cooling/drying appropriately.

components.title: Seasonal coat care and skin hygiene
components.description: Managing heavy shedding, mud fever/scratches, rain rot, and sweaty winter coats without stripping protective oils or trapping dampness under tack.

components.title: Subtle changes and soreness awareness
components.description: Reading localized flinching along the withers, back, girth, or hocks as valuable discomfort data rather than bad behavior, and detecting subtle digital pulses, windpuffs, or body-condition shifts.

intermediate.learning: Manages bathing, seasonal coats, and subtle physical checks with guidance on weather judgment or distinguishing normal coat wear from early pathology.
intermediate.proficient: Independently plans and carries out grooming and bathing suited to weather, coat type, and individual sensitivities, notices subtle coat, skin, hoof, or soreness changes early, and responds or seeks advice appropriately.

subject: rider
name: Blanketing
summary: Selecting, fitting, putting on, and removing horse blankets or sheets safely across different designs.
purpose: Protects horses from weather when needed while preventing rubbing, overheating, or dangerous strap entanglement.
safety: Fasten chest straps first when putting a blanket on and unfasten them last when removing it so a shifting rug never traps the horse's hindquarters.
Never leave leg straps or belly surcingles hanging loose, and never put a standard non-breathable stable or turnout blanket onto a hot, wet, sweating horse before cooling and drying properly.

introductory.overview: Safely putting on, checking strap security, and removing blankets or sheets on a cooperative horse.

components.title: Predictable placement and strap order
components.description: Folding the blanket cleanly onto the back and sliding smoothly into place (avoiding tossing abruptly), fastening chest buckles first, then surcingles/leg straps—and reversing exact order on removal.

components.title: Safe strap length and common mistakes
components.description: Adjusting belly surcingles about a flat hand's width from the barrel and looping leg straps around each hind leg without crossing dangerously tight or sagging low enough to catch a hoof.

introductory.learning: Places and removes a blanket safely with occasional reminders about chest-first fastening, surcingle slack, or untangling leg straps.
introductory.proficient: Independently places, secures, adjusts, and removes common blanket designs calmly in safe strap order without startling the horse or leaving dangling hazards.

intermediate.overview: Matching blanket weight and breathability to horse coat, weather, and sweat status while catching fit pressure and rubs early.

components.title: Cooling, weather, and coat judgment
components.description: Judging whether an unclipped horse with shelter even needs a blanket, using a breathable wicking cooler only while actively drying a damp horse, and removing/switching damp rugs so moisture never chills the back.

components.title: Wither, shoulder, and rub evaluation
components.description: Checking hand-under-wither relief (especially when the head lowers to graze), shoulder gusset freedom, tail-flap cleanliness, and early hair breakage over withers, chest points, or hips.

intermediate.learning: Evaluates blanket weight and fit with occasional guidance on layering, damp coats, or early pressure marks.
intermediate.proficient: Independently selects appropriate sheets, coolers, or weights for coat condition and forecast, confirms the horse is properly cooled and dry before standard blanketing, and corrects rubbing, slipping, or overheating early.

subject: rider
name: Health Monitoring
summary: Assessing a horse's daily appearance, demeanor, and vital signs to establish baselines and spot illness or injury early.
purpose: Early recognition of colic, fever, lameness, or infection improves treatment outcomes and welfare.
safety: Monitor from safe positioning beside the hip or shoulder—especially when checking rectal temperature, flanks, or lower limbs on an uncomfortable horse.
Sanitize thermometers and wash hands between horses to limit contagious barn spread.

introductory.overview: Running a calm daily baseline check of attitude, intake, waste, and outward soundness—and spotting urgent red flags right away.

components.title: Knowing your horse's normal daily baseline
components.description: Observing posture, ear alertness, eye brightness, nostril discharge, water consumption, feed enthusiasm, manure consistency/output, urination posture, and equal weight-bearing across all four feet.

components.title: Recognizing urgent red flags
components.description: Identifying acute colic signs (pawing, flank-watching, repeated lying down/rolling, absent manure), choke (nasal feed/saliva), acute lameness or refusal to bear weight, labored breathing at rest, or active bleeding—and notifying a supervisor or vet promptly.

introductory.learning: Completes daily visual checks and spots major abnormalities with guidance on distinguishing minor quirks from urgent veterinary red flags.
introductory.proficient: Independently performs a systematic daily baseline check, spots abnormal appetite, manure, behavior, heat, swelling, or lameness promptly, and escalates red flags without delay.

intermediate.overview: Measuring vital signs accurately at rest, tracking trends against individual baselines, and relaying clear objective observations to a veterinarian.

components.title: TPR, hydration, and gut sounds
components.description: Safely taking rectal temperature (normal adult range ~99.0–101.5°F / 37.2–38.6°C), pulse (~28–44 bpm), respiration (~8–16 breaths/min), gum color/moistness and capillary refill time (<=2 sec), and listening on all four abdominal quadrants for present vs. quiet gut motility.

components.title: Digital pulses and objective vet reporting
components.description: Palpating digital pulses over the fetlock cleanly to detect pounding warmth in a hoof, and reporting concrete facts (onset, vitals, behavior, last manure) to help a vet triage accurately without attempting diagnosis.

intermediate.learning: Measures vitals and listens for gut sounds with coaching on stethoscope/thermometer technique or interpreting borderline numbers.
intermediate.proficient: Independently and accurately measures temperature, pulse, respiration, mucous membranes, capillary refill, gut sounds, and digital pulses, compares against resting norms, and communicates concise objective findings to a veterinarian.

subject: rider
name: First Aid
summary: Providing safe initial care for minor wounds and stabilizing common equine emergencies while awaiting veterinary guidance.
purpose: Prevents contamination or worsening of injuries and keeps the horse calm and safe until a veterinarian arrives.
safety: Protect human safety first—painful, frightened, or colicking horses can strike, bolt, or drop unpredictably.
Never apply powders, sprays, or heavy ointments to deep wounds or near joints before a veterinarian has evaluated them, and never offer food to a horse showing signs of colic or choke.

intermediate.overview: Assembling a practical first-aid kit, triaging wound location/depth accurately, performing clean initial care, and stabilizing urgent emergencies calmly.

components.title: Wound triage and synovial risk awareness
components.description: Checking wound depth, bleeding rate, and anatomical location—recognizing that tiny punctures near joints, tendon sheaths, hooves, or eyes are high-risk emergencies even with minimal blood—and cleaning superficial abrasions cleanly with saline or mild flush.

components.title: Bleeding control and emergency stabilization
components.description: Applying steady clean gauze/pad pressure for active bleeding without dangerous tourniquets, managing swelling with controlled cold therapy, removing food/water for colic or choke until examined, and keeping clear records for the arriving vet.

intermediate.learning: Performs initial wound cleaning and emergency triage with guidance on synovial risk zones, dressing pressure, or when to avoid bandaging.
intermediate.proficient: Independently maintains practical kit readiness, evaluates wound location and urgency accurately, performs clean initial flushing and pressure/protection safely, recognizes synovial or systemic emergencies immediately, and stabilizes the situation calmly until veterinary care takes over.

introductory.overview: Knowing barn emergency procedures, keeping an injured horse safe while awaiting help, and assisting cleanly with basic superficial rinsing.

components.title: Emergency readiness and safe waiting
components.description: Knowing where emergency contact numbers, halter/lead, and the first-aid kit live; calmly containing or supporting an injured horse without crowding or panicking; and knowing which signs require immediate veterinary/trainer escalation.

components.title: Gentle cold hosing and contamination prevention
components.description: Using slow, clean cool water to gently rinse mud or debris from minor superficial scrapes away from eyes and deep cavities—and keeping hands, dirt, and unapproved salves out of deeper cuts while waiting for guidance.

introductory.learning: Locates emergency contacts/supplies and helps support calm waiting or basic cold rinsing under supervision.
introductory.proficient: Independently locates emergency supplies and contacts, keeps an injured horse calm and safely positioned while summoning qualified help, recognizes wounds or distress requiring immediate care, and performs safe basic cold-water rinsing of minor scrapes without worsening contamination.

subject: rider
name: Administering Medications
summary: Safely preparing and administering prescribed or approved oral medications according to veterinary or label instructions.
purpose: Ensures horses receive accurate doses calmly without stress, aspiration, or wasted medication.
safety: Double-check the five essentials every time: right horse, right medication, right dose, right route, and right time.
Ensure the mouth is clear of hay and grain before any oral syringe—never force paste into a resisting mouth full of food or while the head is tied rigidly upward.

intermediate.overview: Safely verifying prescriptions/labels and delivering oral medications calmly without injury, wasted doses, or creating head-shyness.

components.title: Verification, measuring, and logging
components.description: Confirming veterinarian or label instructions accurately, reading dose syringes or weight scoops carefully, checking expiration and storage conditions, observing competition withdrawal periods where relevant, and logging administration.

components.title: Calm delivery and common mistakes
components.description: Resting a thumb/syringe gently into the toothless interdental space (corner of the mouth) toward the back of the tongue after clearing hay, rather than jabbing bars/teeth or fighting the poll. Avoiding forceful head restraint that escalates future oral aversion.

intermediate.learning: Prepares and delivers oral medications with occasional reminders on label checks, mouth clearing, or keeping delivery low-stress.
intermediate.proficient: Independently verifies instructions, measures accurate oral doses, administers medications calmly via feed or syringe without startling or fighting the horse, confirms intake, and logs treatment accurately.

subject: rider
name: Leg Wraps & Bandaging
summary: Selecting, applying, inspecting, and removing standing wraps, exercise wraps, or basic medical bandages safely.
purpose: Protects lower limbs during travel, rest, exercise, or wound care without causing tendon pressure or circulation issues.
safety: Maintain smooth, uniform wrap tension pulled from front to back across the cannon bone—never yank unevenly across the back tendons or apply tight cord-like creases.
Squat or bend safely ready to step out cleanly; never kneel on both knees beside a horse's legs, and remove/recheck wraps promptly if wet, slipped, or uncomfortable.

intermediate.overview: Selecting suitable padding and wrap types, applying smooth even tension from knee/hock to fetlock, and catching circulation or fit complications early.

components.title: Wrap purpose, padding, and hygiene
components.description: Choosing appropriate materials for standing rest, shipping, exercise support, or clean wound protection—using adequate flat padding beneath elastic bandages and consulting a veterinarian before bandaging acute swelling or open lower-limb wounds.

components.title: Smooth tension and complication checks
components.description: Wrapping smoothly without wrinkles or twisted edges, anchoring over appropriate fetlock support where needed without binding coronary band or knee/hock flexion, checking warmth and comfort regularly, and removing wraps calmly on a schedule.

intermediate.learning: Applies standing or protective wraps with guidance to balance even tension, avoid tendon ridges, or align padding smoothly.
intermediate.proficient: Independently selects, applies, inspects, and removes standing, exercise, or basic medical wraps safely with smooth padding, uniform non-constricting tension, and reliable monitoring for heat, slippage, or swelling.

subject: rider
name: Feeding
summary: Following feeding routines safely, checking feed and water quality, and understanding core equine nutritional principles.
purpose: Supports digestive health and reduces the risk of colic, choke, or barn-aisle conflict during feeding time.
safety: Wait until an overheated, heavily breathing horse has cooled down calmly before offering full grain/concentrate meals, and soak pelleted or senior mashes thoroughly when choke risk is present.
Keep feed rooms securely latched, guard against group aggression at feeding time, and inspect pasture and hay for toxic weeds, mold, or lawn clippings.

introductory.overview: Delivering established rations accurately, keeping clean water accessible, inspecting feed quality, and feeding safely around horses.

components.title: Accurate rationing and calm feeding order
components.description: Measuring feed by weight rather than assuming scoop size equals pounds, delivering hay and concentrates cleanly into sanitary buckets/mangers, and managing barn or pasture spacing so horses do not fight or bolt food.

components.title: Water, forage inspection, and cooling safety
components.description: Providing fresh, ice-free water at safe levels; spotting moldy hay, heated/fermenting grain, baling twine, or toxic plant debris; and offering sensible cool-down time after hard work before large concentrate meals.

introductory.learning: Measures rations and checks water and hay with reminders on exact weights, feed-room security, or safe pasture/stall feeding order.
introductory.proficient: Independently follows feeding instructions accurately by weight/ration, maintains clean water, screens hay and concentrates for spoilage or hazards, and feeds safely without triggering urgency or group conflict.

intermediate.overview: Applying forage-first nutrition principles, adapting routines for workload, dental or metabolic needs, and managing gradual diet changes safely.

components.title: Forage-first digestion and gradual transitions
components.description: Understanding why continuous roughage supports gut health and reduces ulcers/colic, keeping concentrate meals small, soaking high-choke feeds when indicated, and phasing any hay or grain change over 7–14 days.

components.title: Body condition, metabolic risks, and adjustments
components.description: Palpating ribs, crest, and topline for realistic body-condition tracking; recognizing lush pasture or high-starch risks for laminitic or metabolic horses; and collaborating with a vet or equine nutritionist on dietary plans.

intermediate.learning: Applies forage-first principles and evaluates body condition or metabolic flags with guidance on transition pacing or workload adjustments.
intermediate.proficient: Independently evaluates forage quality, hydration, and body condition by sight and feel, carries out gradual feed transitions and choke/metabolic safeguards, and recognizes nutritional warning signs needing professional input.

subject: rider
name: Stable Care
summary: Maintaining clean, dry, hazard-free stalls, shelters, and turnout areas.
purpose: Protects respiratory and hoof health while preventing injuries from sharp hardware, toxic plants, or damaged fencing.
safety: Keep pitchforks, wheelbarrows, hoses, and rakes completely out of horse reach and walkways—never leave tines exposed or stall doors half-latched.
Avoid stirring heavy bedding or aisle dust right in front of stabled horses, and inspect electrical trough heaters, fences, and latches routinely.

introductory.overview: Maintaining clean, dry, low-dust stalls, shelters, waterers, and turnout spaces while spotting physical or respiratory hazards early.

components.title: Sanitary cleaning, bedding, and air quality
components.description: Removing manure and ammonia-soaked bedding thoroughly (especially under hay/water areas), maintaining dry supportive footing, scrubbing water containers before refilling, and prioritizing airflow over heavy dust.

components.title: Daily facility and turnout hazard checks
components.description: Checking stall doors/latches, broken boards, exposed nails, bucket-snap openings that could snag lips/eyelids, loose wire, slick ice/mud bottlenecks, and pasture weeds.

introductory.learning: Cleans stalls and checks waterers with reminders on wet spots, tool placement, dust control, or latch inspection.
introductory.proficient: Independently cleans and beds stalls or shelters cleanly with low dust disruption, scrubs and maintains clean water sources, stores tools safely, and catches and repairs or reports physical hazards.

subject: rider
name: Tack Use, Fit & Care
summary: Putting on, adjusting, safety-checking, removing, and maintaining saddles, bridles, halters, and protective gear.
purpose: Ensures equipment is comfortable for the horse, secure for the rider, and free from worn stitching or unsafe fit.
safety: Inspect weight-bearing stitching, billet straps, cinch/latigo knots, stirrup leathers, and rein hardware before every ride.
Tighten a girth or cinch gradually in stages, verify comfort before mounting, and re-check snugness after walking a few steps.

introductory.overview: Calmly tacking up across familiar English, Western, or bitless setups, completing pre-ride safety checks, and cleaning gear after use.

components.title: Considerate tacking and untacking
components.description: Setting pads and saddle gently down onto a clean back (never dropping hard or letting stirrups/cinches bang elbows), lifting pads slightly into the gullet, checking smooth hair underneath, and offering/removing the bridle/halter calmly clear of teeth and ears.

components.title: Pre-ride safety, snugness, and post-ride care
components.description: Checking billets, latigo knots, stitching, bit/curb hardware, two-finger noseband/throat-latch space, and gradual girth adjustment—followed by wiping sweat/salt and storing tack cleanly.

introductory.learning: Tacks up and completes safety checks with occasional supervision on pad placement, latigo/girth security, or bridle adjustments.
introductory.proficient: Independently and considerately tacks up and untacks a cooperative horse across familiar gear, runs a thorough pre-ride hardware and basic clearance check, and cleans and stores equipment properly.

intermediate.overview: Evaluating static and in-motion tack fit across horse conformation, avoiding comfort workarounds that mask poor fit, and maintaining hidden wear points.

components.title: Functional saddle, pad, and bridle evaluation
components.description: Checking tree width/angle against shoulder movement, spinal/wither clearance when weighted, level seat balance, even sweat patterns vs. dry pressure spots, bit/noseband/chin-strap comfort, and why overly thick pads cannot fix a poorly fitting saddle tree.

components.title: Deep maintenance and fitting referral
components.description: Disassembling tack to spot dry/cracked leather near high-stress bends or rusted D-rings, conditioning appropriately, and recognizing when soreness or asymmetry warrants an equine bodyworker or qualified saddle fitter.

intermediate.learning: Evaluates saddle balance, sweat patterns, and bridle comfort with guidance to distinguish minor pad tweaks from structural fit problems.
intermediate.proficient: Independently assesses saddle, pad, girth/cinch, and bridle fit both standing and under movement, reads rub/sweat/behavioral clues of tack discomfort accurately, maintains deep hardware safety, and seeks professional fitting when needed.
